Academic Reading and Writing Instructional Support
courses.description: This course is designed to support students who are enrolled in Academic Reading and Writing courses. Students who enroll in this course will also be enrolled in the corresponding linked section of ENGL C1000. This course provides instructional support in academic reading, writing and research skills. Students will learn strategies and received guided instruction on assignments in the transfer-level writing intensive course. Co-Requisite: This course is intended to support students in English C1000 if guided self-placement indicates a need or if they wish to build confidence in college composition. Students who enroll in this course will be enrolled in the corresponding, linked section of ENGL C1000.

sections.notes: This course is designed to assist students who want to build confidence in academic reading and writing. It provides support in developing skills and strategies for success in transfer-level writing intensive courses. Students who enroll in this course will also be enrolled in the corresponding, linked section of ENGL C1000.
Must be taken with ENGL C1000 (CRN 7081)

Students enrolling in this section will need effective computer skills with reliable internet access. This course may use an online proctoring service, Honorlock, that requires the use of a webcam during exams and quizzes. There is no charge for the proctoring service, but students may be asked to provide their own webcam. Check the COS online course website at www.siskiyous.edu/online prior to the first day of the semester for specific course information. Must be taken with ENGL C1000 CRN 7155

courses.title: Practical Accounting
courses.instructor: Sherice L Bellamy, Sean P Bowman
courses.description: Provides an introduction to accounting, suitable for students interested in pursuing additional business and accounting courses as well as for students interested in establishing a practical understanding of accounting. BA 0920 includes the application of the double-entry system in the preparation and use of journals, ledgers, worksheets and financial statements. Banking and payroll issues are also explored. (AA)

courses.title: Tutor Training
courses.description: This course introduces the core principles of tutoring for aspiring peer and professional tutors. Students examine inclusive learning theories, culturally responsive communication, and ethical standards that guide effective and professional tutoring. Emphasis is placed on active learning strategies, student-centered practices, and the role of tutoring in promoting confidence and independence. (NDA)

sections.notes: This course emphasizes styles of learning and appropriate techniques in tutoring individually or small groups. (NDA)
